title: Observability metrics + structured logs for bounded autoscaling (desired vs bounded, bound-hit, prediction error)
creator: Allison Grant
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
- Dedicated autoscaling is adding customer-configurable min/max bounds + optional predictive scaling.
- We need deterministic, auditable telemetry to answer:
  1) What did the autoscaler want (requested desired capacity)?
  2) What did it actually set after applying bounds/guardrails (bounded/effective desired)?
  3) How often are customers hitting bounds (especially max-bound saturation)?
  4) Is predictive scaling helping or hurting (forecast accuracy + override reasons)?

Scope (this ticket)
- Define and implement metrics + structured logs for:
  - desired vs bounded replicas (and reason codes)
  - bound-hit counters + time-in-bounded-state
  - prediction error and forecast freshness
- Align naming + label policy with: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metric-naming-for-scaling-and-capacity.json
- Ensure metrics are suitable for per-customer drilldown without exploding cardinality.

Non-goals
- Build full dashboards/alerts (tracked in ENG-22145 + dashboard spec).
- Change autoscaling decision logic beyond emitting telemetry.

Implementation notes
- Primary component: dedicated-autoscaler loop (fleet autoscaler) + capacity-policy evaluation layer.
- Emit metrics from the autoscaler controller process (where desired is computed) to avoid inconsistencies between services.
- For auditability, pair each scale decision with a structured log event that includes inputs + outputs; long-term retention is via audit events (ENG-22146).

Metrics (proposed + shipped)
All metrics must include: deployment_id, region.
- Avoid customer_id as a metric label (high cardinality); include customer_id only in structured logs and audit events. If needed for drilldown, use join via deployment_id -> customer mapping in the dashboard layer.
- Include model_id only where explicitly required; default is to omit.

1) Desired vs bounded capacity
- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.desired_replicas (gauge)
  - Value: raw desired replicas computed before bounds clamp.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, signal_mode=[reactive|predictive|hybrid]

- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.bounded_desired_replicas (gauge)
  - Value: desired replicas after applying min/max bounds + safety clamps.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, signal_mode

- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.capacity_clamp_total (counter)
  - Increments when bounded_desired != desired.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, clamp_type=[min|max|safety_baseline|rate_limit|cooldown], signal_mode
  - Note: clamp_type is mutually exclusive per decision; we emit the highest-precedence clamp reason (per ADR) to keep interpretation consistent.

- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.capacity_clamp_seconds (counter)
  - Adds delta-time spent in a clamped state.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, clamp_type, signal_mode
  - Rationale: counters are easier to alert on than sampling a boolean.

2) Bound-hit counters (explicit min/max)
- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit_total (counter)
  - Increments when clamp_type is min or max.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, bound=[min|max], signal_mode

- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.bound_headroom_replicas (gauge)
  - Value: max_bound - bounded_desired when bounded_desired < max; 0 when at/over max.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region
  - Note: for at-max saturation, headroom=0 is the key signal; when max is unset (legacy), emit -1 and label legacy_policy=true.

3) Prediction error + freshness
- redwood.dedicated.predictor.forecast_age_seconds (gauge)
  - Value: now - forecast_generated_at.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, provider=[internal|partner], status=[ok|stale|missing]

- redwood.dedicated.predictor.forecast_required_total (counter)
  - Increments each autoscaler tick when predictive mode is enabled.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region

- redwood.dedicated.predictor.forecast_used_total (counter)
  - Increments when a valid (non-stale) forecast was used in the decision.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region

- redwood.dedicated.predictor.forecast_error_tokens_per_s (histogram)
  - Value: |predicted - observed| for demand rate (tokens/s) at evaluation time.
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, horizon=[5m|15m|60m]
  - Buckets: tuned to expected Dedicated ranges; keep bucket count modest.
  - Note: If observed rate unavailable, do not emit a sample; emit a structured log with reason.

- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.predictive_override_total (counter)
  - Increments when reactive signals override predicted desired (e.g., queue depth high).
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, override_reason=[queue_depth|saturation|p95_latency|forecast_missing|forecast_stale|guardrail], signal_mode

4) Scale event attribution
- redwood.dedicated.autoscaler.scale_event_total (counter)
  - Increments on every applied scale action (replica count change).
  - Labels: deployment_id, region, direction=[up|down|none], reason=[reactive|predictive|bounds|min_safety|cooldown|rate_limit], signal_mode
  - Note: direction=none is emitted when the controller evaluates but makes no changes; useful for rate calculations.

Structured logs (shipped)
- Emit a single JSON log per evaluation tick, sampled at 1:1 for pilots and 1:N for GA (configurable).
- Event name: dedicated_autoscaler_decision
- Required fields (log payload):
  - timestamp, deployment_id, region, signal_mode
  - desired_replicas_raw, desired_replicas_bounded
  - min_bound, max_bound, effective_min, effective_max
  - clamp_type (same taxonomy as metrics)
  - inputs: queue_depth, utilization, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_s_observed
  - forecast: predicted_tokens_per_s, horizon, age_seconds, provider, status
  - decision: scale_delta, new_target_replicas
  - why: list of short reason strings (bounded to <=5, each <=64 chars)
- Guardrails:
  - No customer-provided PII or request content.
  - Ensure reason strings are from a fixed enum or well-controlled templates to avoid unbounded cardinality.

Acceptance criteria
- Metrics emitted in at least one canary region (us-east-1) for pilot deployments.
- Metrics follow naming + label conventions; validated by observability lint checks.
- Dashboards can plot desired vs bounded replicas and bound-hit rate using only deployment_id + region.
- Structured logs include both requested desired + bounded desired + clamp reason.
- Verified in simulation/replay harness (ENG-22147) that clamp counters move as expected across scenarios (min clamp, max clamp, forecast missing, stale forecast).

Testing / validation
- Unit tests:
  - clamp reason precedence mapping
  - emission of bound_hit_total only on min/max clamps
  - forecast staleness -> forecast_used_total not incremented, override reason increments
- Integration test:
  - run autoscaler tick with mock predictor returning null/stale/valid
  - ensure logs include required fields and metrics are emitted

Links
- Confluence metric naming standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metric-naming-for-scaling-and-capacity.json
- Related PR (implementation): sources/github/redwood/pr-48241-add-metrics-desired-vs-bounded-capacity.json
- Alerting follow-up: ENG-22145
- Audit events follow-up: ENG-22146

Rollout notes
- Pilot: metrics at 1:1, logs at 1:1; verify no cardinality blowups.
- GA: logs sampled down (default 1:20) except when clamp_type=max or unmet_min_capacity (force 1:1 for debugging).

2025-06-24 (Vanessa Ortiz): +1 on clamp_type taxonomy. Make sure max-bound saturation is easy to alert on (either time-in-state or repeated clamp events).

2025-06-27 (Sergio Costa): For dashboards we’ll need a stable way to display min/max configured values. If those aren’t metric labels, can we emit min_bound/max_bound as gauges (deployment_id, region) so we don’t need to call the control plane for every panel?

2025-06-28 (Caleb Johnson): Added min_bound_replicas and max_bound_replicas gauges (deployment_id, region) behind the same flag. Not included as labels anywhere. Will wire into the Grafana spec so it’s a single datasource.

2025-07-03 (Rafael Mendes): Please include an explicit metric for forecast_age_seconds and forecast_used_total. During incidents we need a fast way to tell whether predictive mode is silently falling back to reactive due to staleness.

2025-07-10 (Caleb Johnson): PR up: pr-48241. Includes desired/bounded gauges, clamp counters, forecast freshness metrics, and dedicated_autoscaler_decision structured log event. Also added a lint check to reject customer_id labels.
2025-07-16 (Miles Thornton): Reviewed PR. One request: ensure clamp_type is single-valued and matches ADR precedence; otherwise dashboards will be ambiguous when multiple guardrails apply.
2025-07-17 (Caleb Johnson): Updated implementation to choose the highest-precedence clamp reason only (max > min > safety_baseline > cooldown > rate_limit). Added tests. Ready for re-review.

2025-07-23 (Vanessa Ortiz): After pilot incident, we need a way to spot null forecasts causing unsafe downscale attempts. The structured log event should include forecast.status and the final bounded desired; this will help validate the hotfix behavior.
2025-08-02 (Allison Grant): Marking done after merge + canary verification in us-east-1. Dashboard/alert work continues in ENG-22145, and audit retention is tracked in ENG-22146.
